summary: Feed s156_double to IDS is degraded: 9.1% duplicate packets (218/2404) and 50% untagged traffic with required VLAN 20 completely missing. IDS detection coverage is reduced due to wasted processing on duplicates and blind spot for VLAN 20.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is aggregating the same traffic from two sources without deduplication - feed name 's156_double' and 9.1% duplicates indicate dual SPAN/TAP feeds or both sides of a link mirrored to same tool port without dedup enabled.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/memory reprocessing identical packets, inflates flow/state tables and alert counts, risks false positives and missed true positives due to unnecessary load and skewed analytics.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication within a short time window to drop identical packets before delivery to IDS, eliminating 9% overhead while preserving unique flows.

findings.root_cause: VLAN tags are being stripped upstream - likely SPAN configured as access port instead of trunk or packet broker stripping 802.1Q. 50% of packets are untagged and required VLAN 20 is never seen despite IDS requiring VLANs 10 and 20.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS loses segment context for half the traffic and is completely blind to VLAN 20. Cannot apply VLAN-aware policies, correlate tenant traffic, or detect lateral movement/segmentation violations in VLAN 20.

recommended_fix.why: Configure source SPAN/TAP as 802.1Q trunk and set packet broker to preserve/pass VLAN tags 10 and 20 to the IDS tool port to restore full VLAN visibility.
